cards.hearing: You may be hearing that the Fed, which sets short-term interest rates, just raised rates for the first time in years.
cards.why: That can nudge up the cost of things like a car loan, a credit card balance, or a new mortgage, since borrowing tends to cost a little more when rates go up.
cards.but: But rates moving up and down is exactly the kind of thing your plan was built to handle.
cards.story: Picture a thermostat in a house. Sometimes it clicks up, sometimes down, and the family still eats dinner and goes to bed at the same time every night. Rate moves are the thermostat. Your routine, the plan, stays the same.
say: We built your plan expecting rates to move in both directions.
This is normal weather, not a reason to redo the plan.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing about rising tension overseas, with reports of a bomb plot tied to Iran at a UK air base used by U.S. forces, as the U.S.-Iran conflict continues to make headlines.
cards.why: This matters because tension between countries can push oil prices higher, and oil prices flow into the cost of gas, diesel, and eventually the shipping costs baked into groceries and everyday goods.
cards.but: But a scary overseas headline moving markets for a morning is not a reason to rewrite a plan built for years, not days.
cards.story: Think of a sudden thunderstorm on a long road trip. You slow down, you stay alert, but you don't turn the car around and cancel the whole trip. The destination hasn't changed.
say: We watch headlines like this closely, but we don't drive your plan off them.
One stormy morning doesn't cancel a trip we planned for years.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that a major interest rate, the one that influences mortgages, car loans, and business borrowing, has climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades.
cards.why: This matters because higher rates can mean pricier mortgages, car payments, and credit card bills for a lot of households.
cards.but: But a rate hitting a new high on a chart is not something you have to react to personally, especially if your plan already expected some bumps along the way.
cards.story: Imagine your neighborhood raising the toll on the highway you rarely use. It changes the drive for some people, but it doesn't touch the route you've already mapped out for your own trip.
say: Higher rates get headlines, but your plan was built to handle stretches like this.
We don't chase every rate move, we stick with the road we already mapped.
